body: European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency (CINEA)
title: Innovation Fund - General decarbonisation, Large-Scale Projects (INNOVFUND-2025-NZT-GENERAL-LSP)
deadline: IF25 NZT closed 23 April 2026; Innovation Fund calls typically open at the end of the year
eligibility_text: Only projects with a capital expenditure as indicated below will be eligible under this call: INNOVFUND-2025-NZT-GENERAL-LSP - Capital expenditure above EUR 100 000 000. [...] In order to be eligible, the applicants (beneficiaries and affiliated entities) must: be legal entities (public or private bodies); be established in one of the eligible countries: any country in the world. [...] The maximum grant amount must not exceed 60 % of the relevant costs. Only projects with relevant costs higher than zero are eligible. [...] 'Capital expenditure' means all project costs for project development or construction, that are incurred or to be incurred before the project's entry into operation.
description: Innovation Fund general decarbonisation, LARGE-scale lot. The lot is defined purely by project size: CAPEX above EUR 100m. That threshold, not the technology scope, is what separates it from the medium-scale and small-scale lots, which share the same scope and the same eligibility rules. Budget EUR 1.2bn under IF25.
administering_body: European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency (CINEA)

body: European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency (CINEA)
title: Innovation Fund - General decarbonisation, Medium-Scale Projects (INNOVFUND-2025-NZT-GENERAL-MSP)
deadline: IF25 NZT closed 23 April 2026; Innovation Fund calls typically open at the end of the year
eligibility_text: Only projects with a capital expenditure as indicated below will be eligible under this call: INNOVFUND-2025-NZT-GENERAL-MSP - Capital expenditure above EUR 20 000 000 and up to EUR 100 000 000. [...] In order to be eligible, the applicants (beneficiaries and affiliated entities) must: be legal entities (public or private bodies); be established in one of the eligible countries: any country in the world. [...] The maximum grant amount must not exceed 60 % of the relevant costs. [...] This call reflects the revised EU ETS Directive 2003/87 which extends the Innovation Fund to medium-scale projects and to the maritime, buildings and road transport sectors.
description: Innovation Fund general decarbonisation, MEDIUM-scale lot: CAPEX above EUR 20m and up to EUR 100m. The medium-scale band exists only because the revised ETS Directive extended the Fund to it; it is bounded on both sides, which is what separates it from the large-scale lot above and the small-scale lot below. Budget EUR 300m under IF25.
administering_body: European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency (CINEA)

body: European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency (CINEA)
title: Innovation Fund - General decarbonisation, Small-Scale Projects (INNOVFUND-2025-NZT-GENERAL-SSP)
deadline: IF25 NZT closed 23 April 2026; Innovation Fund calls typically open at the end of the year
eligibility_text: Only projects with a capital expenditure as indicated below will be eligible under this call: INNOVFUND-2025-NZT-GENERAL-SSP - Capital expenditure above EUR 2 500 000 and up to EUR 20 000 000. [...] In order to be eligible, the applicants (beneficiaries and affiliated entities) must: be legal entities (public or private bodies); be established in one of the eligible countries: any country in the world. [...] The maximum grant amount must not exceed 60 % of the relevant costs.
description: Innovation Fund general decarbonisation, SMALL-scale lot: CAPEX above EUR 2.5m and up to EUR 20m. This is the only general-decarbonisation lot a company with a sub-EUR-20m project can enter, and the lowest CAPEX floor in the regime other than the manufacturing and pilot topics. Budget EUR 100m under IF25.
administering_body: European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency (CINEA)

body: European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency (CINEA)
title: Innovation Fund - Clean-tech manufacturing (INNOVFUND-2025-NZT-CLEAN-TECH-MANUFACTURING)
deadline: IF25 NZT closed 23 April 2026; Innovation Fund calls typically open at the end of the year
eligibility_text: Capital expenditure above EUR 2 500 000. [...] Activities that can be funded (scope): Construction and operation of manufacturing facilities to produce specific components for: Renewable energy: facilities producing components for photovoltaics, concentrated solar power, onshore and offshore wind power, ocean energy, geothermal, solar thermal, and other renewable energy systems, including their connection to the electricity/heat grid. Electrolysers and fuel cells: manufacturing of electrolysers and fuel cells for hydrogen production and consumption. Energy storage solutions: production of batteries and other storage solutions for stationary and mobile use, covering both intra-day and long duration storage. Heat pumps: development and production of heat pumps. [...] The topic also targets the manufacturing of components and materials (except mining activities) that are a significant factor in the final equipment's performance and/or cost. [...] Under this topic, the use of innovative components, including the final equipment, in power/heat generation, energy storage, or production and consumption of hydrogen will not be supported. [...] Only projects that have not reached financial close at proposal submission date can be funded.
description: Innovation Fund clean-tech MANUFACTURING lot. Distinguishing feature within the regime: it funds building the factory, not deploying the technology - and explicitly excludes USING the equipment in generation, storage or hydrogen, which is what the general-decarbonisation lots fund. Mining is excluded; the project must not have reached financial close at submission. CAPEX floor EUR 2.5m, no ceiling. Budget EUR 1bn under IF25.
administering_body: European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency (CINEA)

body: European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency (CINEA)
title: Innovation Fund - Pilot projects (INNOVFUND-2025-NZT-PILOTS)
deadline: IF25 NZT closed 23 April 2026; Innovation Fund calls typically open at the end of the year
eligibility_text: Capital expenditure above EUR 2 500 000. [...] The objective of this topic is to support highly innovative, disruptive or breakthrough technologies that enable deep decarbonisation needed for achieving climate neutrality. Activities that can be funded (scope): construction and operation of pilot projects that focus on validating, testing and optimising highly innovative, deep decarbonisation solutions in all sectors eligible for Innovation Fund support. [...] The objective of the pilot project must focus on testing and validating the innovative technology at pilot scale, but must not yet reach large scale demonstration or first-of-a-kind commercial production. [...] The applicant must present a strategy for the technology to progress to large-scale demonstration / deployment or first-of-a-kind commercial production, after demonstration at pilot scale.
description: Innovation Fund PILOT lot. Distinguishing feature within the regime: it is the only lot that requires the project to stop SHORT of commercial scale - a proposal that has already reached large-scale demonstration or first-of-a-kind commercial production is ineligible here and belongs in a general-decarbonisation lot. It also carries the regime's highest GHG-avoidance weighting threshold (75% versus the standard). CAPEX floor EUR 2.5m. Budget EUR 300m under IF25.
administering_body: European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency (CINEA)

body: European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency (CINEA)
title: Innovation Fund - Electric vehicle battery cell manufacturing (INNOVFUND-BATT)
deadline: IF24 Battery call awarded November 2025; successor activity runs through the Battery Booster Facility announced July 2026
eligibility_text: Projects must focus on battery cell manufacturing suitable for electric-vehicle applications, be in the ramp-up phase at the opening of the call, represent the applicant's first full commercial-scale production project for electric vehicle battery cells globally, and have a planned annual production capacity of at least 10 GWh.
description: Innovation Fund dedicated ELECTRIC VEHICLE BATTERY CELL lot. Distinguishing feature within the regime, and the sharpest single eligibility threshold in it: a planned annual production capacity of at least 10 GWh, plus a first-of-its-kind test applied to the APPLICANT GLOBALLY (not to the technology) - a company that already runs commercial-scale EV cell production anywhere in the world is excluded. No other Innovation Fund lot applies a capacity floor.
note: Confidence medium: the four conditions are reproduced from the Commission's own call summaries for the IF24 battery call rather than from a single verbatim eligibility clause read off the call fiche PDF. The 10 GWh figure and the global-first-project test are consistently stated across climate.ec.europa.eu and cinea.ec.europa.eu.
administering_body: European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency (CINEA)

body: European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency (CINEA) / European Hydrogen Bank
title: Innovation Fund - European Hydrogen Bank competitive bidding (auction)
deadline: Third auction ran 4 December 2025 - 19 February 2026; IF26 hydrogen auction draft terms and conditions were in public consultation until 24 August 2026
eligibility_text: Projects selected under the auction will receive support in the form of a fixed premium payment upon verified and certified production of hydrogen (EUR/kg RFNBO hydrogen), for a maximum period of 10 years of operation. [...] The third auction covered three topics: a topic for RFNBO hydrogen production; a topic for RFNBO and/or electrolytic low-carbon hydrogen production; and a topic for RFNBO and/or electrolytic low-carbon hydrogen production supplied to the Maritime or Aviation sectors.
description: European Hydrogen Bank auction. Distinguishing feature within the Innovation Fund regime: it is not a grant call at all but a COMPETITIVE AUCTION - bidders compete on a requested subsidy in EUR per kilogram, and the award is a fixed premium paid only against verified certified RFNBO production over up to 10 years of operation. Payout is therefore contingent on delivered volume rather than fixed at signature, which is why award amounts recorded against this lot are ceilings.
note: Confidence medium: topic structure and the fixed-premium mechanism are quoted from the Commission's auction pages; the per-auction maximum bid price ceiling is set in each round's Terms and Conditions and is not reproduced here because it changes every round and no single current value would be true.
administering_body: European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency (CINEA) / European Hydrogen Bank

body: European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency (CINEA) / European Hydrogen Bank
title: Innovation Fund IF24 Hydrogen Bank auction - Maritime topic
deadline: IF24 auction opened 3 December 2024 and closed 20 February 2025; superseded by the third auction (Dec 2025 - Feb 2026), which carries a Maritime or Aviation topic
eligibility_text: The IF24 auction established a novel dedicated budget of EUR 200 million for projects with off-takers in the maritime sector. Successful bidders receive a fixed premium payment upon production of certified and verified hydrogen (EUR/kg RFNBO hydrogen), for a maximum period of 10 years of operation. [...] The successor third auction carries a topic for RFNBO and/or electrolytic low-carbon hydrogen production supplied to the Maritime or Aviation sectors, with EUR 300 million available.
description: The maritime sub-topic of the IF24 Hydrogen Bank auction. Distinguishing feature within the Innovation Fund regime: eligibility turns on WHO BUYS THE HYDROGEN - the off-taker must be in the maritime sector - rather than on project size or technology. Winning bids in this topic were EUR 0.45/kg and EUR 1.88/kg. This is the only Norwegian row in the corpus that shares a regime with siblings.
note: Recorded as superseded, not closed: the maritime route still exists as the Maritime-or-Aviation topic of the current auction round, so a founder is not being pointed at a dead end, but the IF24 round itself has ended.
administering_body: European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency (CINEA) / European Hydrogen Bank

body: European Innovation Council and SMEs Executive Agency (EISMEA)
title: EIC Accelerator
deadline: Short proposals continuous, batched every first Tuesday of the month 17:00 Brussels; full-proposal cut-offs 2026: 07/01, 04/03, 06/05, 08/07, 02/09, 04/11
eligibility_text: Single start-up or SME (including spin-outs). Small mid-caps (up to 499 employees). Natural persons or legal entities willing to set up an SME or a mid-cap. [...] Applicants from EU Member States and countries associated to the Horizon Europe programme. Applicants from third countries may relocate their company in order to become eligible. [...] Applicants must have an innovative, game changing product, service or business model with the potential to create new markets or disrupt existing ones, at TRL 6-8.
description: EIC Accelerator: blended finance for single companies taking a validated technology to market. Grant up to EUR 2.5m, optionally combined with EIC Fund equity of EUR 0.5m-10m. Distinguishing feature within the EIC regime: SINGLE-applicant only (no consortium), late TRL 6-8, and the only EIC track open to small mid-caps up to 499 employees.
administering_body: European Innovation Council and SMEs Executive Agency (EISMEA)

body: European Innovation Council and SMEs Executive Agency (EISMEA)
title: EIC Pathfinder
deadline: EIC Pathfinder Open: 12 May 2026; EIC Pathfinder Challenges: 28 October 2026
eligibility_text: Consortia of at least three different independent legal entities, with at least one legal entity established in a Member State and at least two other independent legal entities, each established in different Member States or Associated Countries. [...] Single applicants, small and larger consortia (two partners) are eligible for EIC Pathfinder Challenges only. [...] Consortia from EU Member States and countries associated to the Horizon Europe programme. [...] Supports the early stage development of future technologies (e.g. various activities at low TRL 1-4), up to proof of concept.
description: EIC Pathfinder: early-stage research on future and emerging technologies. Distinguishing feature within the EIC regime: the EARLIEST TRL band (1-4) and the only EIC track that normally REQUIRES a three-party cross-border consortium; single applicants are admitted under Challenges only.
administering_body: European Innovation Council and SMEs Executive Agency (EISMEA)

body: European Innovation Council and SMEs Executive Agency (EISMEA)
title: EIC Transition
eligibility_text: Single legal entities established in a Member State or an Associated Country ('mono-beneficiary') if you are a start-up, SME or research performing organisation. Small consortia of two independent legal entities from two different Member States or Associated Countries. Consortia of minimum three and maximum five independent legal entities ('multi-beneficiary'). [...] Your proposal must build on results already achieved within an eligible project that are, at least, at experimental proof of concept (TRL 3 completed) or, ideally, technology validated in the lab level (TRL 4). [...] Eligible source projects: EIC Pathfinder projects; European Research Council Proof of Concept projects; Research and Innovation Actions; European Defence Fund projects (civil applications only); Research Infrastructure-funded actions.
description: EIC Transition: maturing a proof of concept from an earlier EU-funded project towards market readiness. Distinguishing feature within the EIC regime: eligibility is GATED ON PRIOR EU FUNDING - the proposal must build on results from a named eligible source project (Pathfinder, ERC PoC, RIA, EDF civil, Research Infrastructures) - and the consortium is capped at five partners.
administering_body: European Innovation Council and SMEs Executive Agency (EISMEA)

body: European Innovation Council Fund (managed for the Commission by EISMEA)
title: EIC Fund (equity)
deadline: Follows the EIC Accelerator cut-offs; STEP Scale Up has its own rolling process
eligibility_text: The EIC Fund makes direct equity investments in companies selected through the EIC Accelerator, ranging between EUR 0.5 million and EUR 10 million. Under the 2026 EIC Work Programme there are no preconditions to apply for equity only support. [...] The EIC STEP Scale Up scheme provides investments of between EUR 10 and EUR 30 million per company, aiming to leverage private co-investment and achieve financing rounds of EUR 50 to EUR 150 million or more. [...] In specific areas of strategic technology a company may be excluded if it is controlled by entities outside the EU or the associated countries, or the Commission may require that the investment agreement includes appropriate safeguards.
description: EIC Fund: the equity arm of the EIC, investing directly on the Commission's behalf. Distinguishing feature within the EIC regime: it is the only EQUITY instrument (the other three tracks are grants), its ticket band is EUR 0.5m-10m rising to EUR 10m-30m under STEP Scale Up, and it carries a foreign-control exclusion the grant tracks do not.
note: Confidence medium rather than high: the ticket bands and the 'no preconditions for equity-only' rule are quoted from the EIC 2026 Work Programme as summarised on eic.ec.europa.eu, not from a single verbatim eligibility section on one page. /eic-investments/eic-fund_en returns 404; the live path is /eic-fund_en.
administering_body: European Innovation Council Fund (managed for the Commission by EISMEA)
